content.title: Categorization of risk factors for venous thromboembolism based on the risk of recurrence over the long-term

risk_categories.name: Low (<3% per year)
risk_categories.description: Major transient or reversible factors associated with >10-fold increased risk for the index VTE event (compared to patients without the risk factor).
examples: Surgery with general anaesthesia for >30 min
Confined to bed in hospital (only 'bathroom privileges') for ≥3 days due to an acute illness, or acute exacerbation of a chronic illness

risk_categories.name: Intermediate (3–8% per year)
risk_categories.description: Transient or reversible factors associated with ≤10-fold increased risk for first (index) VTE.
examples: Admission to hospital for <3 days with an acute illness
Confined to bed out of hospital for ≥3 days with an acute illness
Leg injury (without fracture) associated with reduced mobility for ≥3 days
risk_categories.no_identifiable_risk_factor: Listed as a possible category within intermediate section

risk_categories.name: High (>8% per year)
risk_categories.description: Persistent or strong risk factors associated with high long-term recurrence risk.
examples: One or more previous episodes of VTE in the absence of a major transient or reversible factor

footnotes: If anticoagulation is discontinued after the first 3 months (based on data from Baglin et al. and Iorio et al.).
The categorization of risk factors for the index VTE event is in line with that proposed by the International Society on Thrombosis and Haemostasis (ISTH).
The present Guidelines avoid terms such as 'provoked', 'unprovoked', or 'idiopathic' VTE.
content.source_notes: Table organizes risk factors by estimated long-term recurrence risk and gives examples and persistent risk categories.
